item.title: Matsusaka Beef: Japan's Most Luxurious Wagyu — Guide
item.description: Matsusaka beef is among the most prestigious and expensive wagyu in Japan, ranked with Kobe and Omi at the very top of the country’s beef. It comes from virgin female cattle raised with legendary care in and around the castle town of Matsusaka — famously massaged and, in old lore, given beer to stimulate appetite — over an unusually long fattening period that produces an extraordinarily fine, low-melting marble that dissolves on the tongue.

item.title: Omi Beef: Japan's Oldest Wagyu Brand — Guide
item.description: Omi beef is Japan’s oldest wagyu brand, raised in Shiga’s mild lake basin for over 400 years and famously supplied to the Tokugawa shoguns as ‘medicinal’ miso-cured beef in an age when eating meat was officially taboo. Counted with Kobe and Matsusaka among Japan’s top three wagyu, it is prized for silken, fine-grained marbling with a low melting point that dissolves on the tongue, and Shiga serves it every way: bubbling sukiyaki in century-old restaurants, charcoal-grilled steak, shabu-shabu, and affordable lunchtime beef bowls in the castle towns of Hikone and Omihachiman.
